## Summary

The bug was in `src/spyOn.ts`. When `spyOn` was called on a method inherited from the prototype:

1. `getDescriptor` would walk the prototype chain to find the original descriptor.
2. `reassign(spy)` would create an own property on the instance pointing at the spy.
3. On restore, `reassign(original)` would re-define an own property pointing at the original function — leaving a leaked own property that shadowed the prototype method.

### Fix

Two coordinated changes in `src/spyOn.ts`:

1. **`getDescriptor`** now returns a tuple `[descriptor, isOwn]` so callers know whether the descriptor was found on the instance itself (`true`) or via the prototype chain (`false`).

2. **`restore`** checks the flag: if the method was inherited (`!isOwnDescriptor`), it `delete`s the own property it had created — letting the original prototype method become visible again. Otherwise, it falls back to the previous behaviour of restoring via `define`/`reassign`.

## Summary

The bug was in `src/spyOn.ts`. When `spyOn` was called on a method inherited from the prototype:

1. `getDescriptor` would walk the prototype chain to find the original descriptor.
2. `reassign(spy)` would create an own property on the instance pointing at the spy.
3. On restore, `reassign(original)` would re-define an own property pointing at the original function — leaving a leaked own property that shadowed the prototype method.

### Fix

Two coordinated changes in `src/spyOn.ts`:

1. **`getDescriptor`** now returns a tuple `[descriptor, isOwn]` so callers know whether the descriptor was found on the instance itself (`true`) or via the prototype chain (`false`).

2. **`restore`** checks the flag: if the method was inherited (`!isOwnDescriptor`), it `delete`s the own property it had created — letting the original prototype method become visible again. Otherwise, it falls back to the previous behaviour of restoring via `define`/`reassign`.
